source.section: Form IL-1040 Line 2; Instructions PDF page 7, Line 2; Schedule M Instructions PDF page 4, Lines 34 and 35; Form IL-1040 PDF page 1, Lines 1-19; Instructions PDF page 8, Lines 10-12; rate Instructions PDF page 1; Line 10a chart and Income Exceptions, Instructions PDF page 8

worked: Federal AGI = wages (person 0) 42,850.00 = 42,850.00. Federal taxable income = 42,850.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 27,100.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Illinois starts from federal AGI). Form IL-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 42,850.00. Line 2 federally tax-exempt interest 10,000.00. Line 3 other additions 0.00. Line 4 = 52,850.00. Line 5 0.00. Lines 6 and 7 0.00. Line 8 = 0.00. Line 9 base income = 52,850.00 - 0.00 = 52,850.00. Income Exceptions: federal AGI 42,850.00 is not greater than 250,000.00, so the allowance stands. Line 10a 2,850.00. Line 10b 0.00. Lines 10c and 10d 0.00. Line 10 = 2,850.00. Line 11 net income = 52,850.00 - 2,850.00 = 50,000.00. Line 12 tax = 50,000.00 x 4.95% = 2,475.0000. Lines 13-18 0.00 (no credits in the projection). Line 19 state income tax = 2,475.00. Line 2 adds back both, because Illinois's own bonds are not exempt as a class. A bond on the Line 34 or 35 list would come off on Schedule M; the projection cannot tell which, so none do.
accepted_approximations: All municipal bond interest is taxed. Illinois adds back all federally tax-exempt interest and exempts only listed obligations (Schedule M Lines 34 and 35), which a projection cannot tell from others.
